docs.title: A Water Quality Modeling Framework
docs.text:
ClearWater is a modular water quality modeling framework developed by the U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC). It couples a riverine hydrodynamic transport engine with pluggable water quality simulation modules for temperature, general constituents, and nutrient cycling.

ClearWater consists of three components:

  • ClearWater-Riverine -- Hydrodynamic transport framework that reads HEC-RAS output and drives constituent transport through the river network.
  • ClearWater-Modules -- Water quality process modules, including:
    • TSM -- Temperature Simulation Module (energy balance)
    • GSM -- General Constituents Simulation Module (first-order decay/settling for arbitrary constituents)
    • NSM1 -- Nutrient Simulation Module (algae, nitrogen, phosphorus, carbon, dissolved oxygen, pathogens, alkalinity)
  • ClearWater-Data -- Data access and storage layer built on xarray, providing a VariableRegistry and chunked zarr I/O for memory-efficient simulation.

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
• Modular architecture: Each water quality process is a self-contained Process class with explicit inputs, outputs, and configuration. Processes can be composed in any combination.
  • Memory-efficient: Chunked time-stepping with zarr-backed data stores allows long simulations without holding the full time history in RAM.
  • Config-driven: Model assembly from YAML configuration files via ProcessFactory.
  • Extensible: Adding a new water quality process requires implementing a single Process subclass and registering it.

docs.title: Citation
docs.text:
When using ClearWater in publications, please cite:

Steissberg, T.E., et al. ClearWater: A Modular Water Quality Modeling Framework. U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center, Vicksburg, MS.

docs.title: Theory
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This section presents the theoretical foundations underlying the ClearWater framework, including hydrodynamic transport, surface energy balance for temperature, water quality kinetics, and the numerical methods used for integration.

docs.title: Hydrodynamic Theory
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will present the governing equations for hydrodynamic transport in ClearWater-Riverine, including the 2D advection-diffusion equation, how flow fields and geometry are extracted from HEC-RAS, and the finite-volume discretization on unstructured meshes.

docs.title: Water Quality Kinetics Theory
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will present the theoretical basis for water quality reaction kinetics used in NSM1 and GSM, including the Arrhenius temperature correction (rate = rate_20 * theta^(T - 20)), stoichiometric coupling between state variables, Monod and Michaelis-Menten growth formulations, and light attenuation models for algal photosynthesis.

docs.title: Numerical Methods
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will describe the numerical methods used in ClearWater, including the forward Euler time integration for reaction kinetics, operator splitting between transport and reactions, spatial chunking strategies for large meshes, and stability constraints on time step selection.

docs.title: Temperature and Energy Balance Theory
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will present the theoretical basis for the temperature simulation, including the complete surface energy balance equation, formulations for each heat flux component (shortwave, longwave, evaporative, conductive, sediment), and the equilibrium temperature approach.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This section provides detailed documentation for each ClearWater component: ClearWater-Riverine (hydrodynamics), TSM (temperature), GSM (general constituent transport), NSM1 (nutrient simulation), and ClearWater-Data (data management).

docs.title: ClearWater-Data
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This section covers ClearWater-Data, the data management layer that provides the VariableRegistry and chunked Zarr-based data storage for efficient large-scale water quality simulations.

docs.title: ClearWater-Data Overview
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will describe the ClearWater-Data package, including its role in managing simulation variables, providing a centralized registry for state variables and parameters, and handling I/O through chunked Zarr data stores for memory-efficient processing of large meshes and long time series.

docs.title: VariableRegistry
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will document the VariableRegistry API, including how to define, register, and look up state variables and parameters. It will cover variable metadata (units, default values, bounds), the registration pattern used by Process subclasses, and how the registry connects to the Model orchestrator.

docs.title: ChunkedZarrDataStore
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will document the ChunkedZarrDataStore, which provides chunked, out-of-core storage for simulation data using the Zarr format. It will cover configuration options, chunking strategies for spatial and temporal dimensions, and how to read/write simulation results efficiently.

docs.title: General Constituent Simulation Module (GSM)
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This section covers the General Constituent Simulation Module (GSM), which simulates transport and fate of conservative or simple first-order decay constituents with optional settling.

docs.title: GSM Configuration
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will document the configuration options for the General Constituent Simulation Module, including decay rate coefficients, settling velocities, and initial/boundary concentrations.

docs.title: GSM Overview
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will describe the General Constituent Simulation Module, which provides a simple framework for modeling constituents with first-order decay and/or settling. GSM is suitable for tracers, sediment, and any constituent that does not require the full nutrient kinetics of NSM1.

docs.title: Nutrient Simulation Module (NSM1)
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This section covers the Nutrient Simulation Module Level 1 (NSM1), which simulates coupled nutrient cycling, algal growth, dissolved oxygen dynamics, and pathogen fate. NSM1 tracks multiple interacting state variables including algae, nitrogen species, phosphorus species, carbon species, CBOD, dissolved oxygen, pathogens, and alkalinity.

docs.title: Alkalinity
docs.text:
This page is under development.

Documents the alkalinity process, corresponding to dAlkdt in v1 nsm1/processes.py. This page will cover how alkalinity is affected by nitrification, denitrification, algal uptake, and carbon dioxide exchange, and its role in buffering pH in the water column.

docs.title: Benthic Algae
docs.text:
This page is under development.

Documents the benthic algae (periphyton) process, corresponding to dAbdt in v1 nsm1/processes.py. This page will cover benthic algal growth, respiration, density-dependent limitations, and the influence of benthic algae on nutrient uptake and dissolved oxygen at the sediment-water interface.

docs.title: Carbon
docs.text:
This page is under development.

Documents the carbon processes, corresponding to dPOCdt, dDOCdt, and dDICdt in v1 nsm1/processes.py. This page will cover particulate organic carbon (POC) dissolution and settling, dissolved organic carbon (DOC) oxidation, and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) dynamics including CO2 exchange and alkalinity coupling.

docs.title: Carbonaceous BOD
docs.text:
This page is under development.

Documents the carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand (CBOD) process, corresponding to dCBODdt in v1 nsm1/processes.py. This page will cover CBOD oxidation kinetics, settling, and the CBOD contribution to dissolved oxygen consumption.

docs.title: Dissolved Oxygen
docs.text:
This page is under development.

Documents the dissolved oxygen (DOX) budget, corresponding to dDOXdt in v1 nsm1/processes.py. This page will detail the nine source/sink terms in the DO balance: atmospheric reaeration, photosynthesis, respiration, nitrification, CBOD oxidation, sediment oxygen demand (SOD), and carbon oxidation, along with the Arrhenius temperature corrections applied to each rate.

docs.title: Floating Algae
docs.text:
This page is under development.

Documents the floating algae (phytoplankton) process, corresponding to dApdt in v1 nsm1/processes.py. This page will cover algal growth (light- and nutrient-limited), respiration, settling, and the effects of floating algae on dissolved oxygen, nitrogen, and phosphorus cycling.

docs.title: Nitrogen Cycle
docs.text:
This page is under development.

Documents the nitrogen cycle processes, corresponding to dOrgNdt, dNH4dt, and dNO3dt in v1 nsm1/processes.py. This page will cover organic nitrogen hydrolysis, ammonia nitrification, nitrate denitrification, algal uptake and release, atmospheric deposition, and sediment fluxes for each nitrogen species.

docs.title: NSM1 Overview
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will provide an overview of the NSM1 module, including a state variable interaction diagram showing the coupled relationships between floating algae, benthic algae, nitrogen (OrgN, NH4, NO3), phosphorus (OrgP, TIP), carbon (POC, DOC, DIC), CBOD, dissolved oxygen, pathogens, and alkalinity. It will also describe the Arrhenius temperature correction used across all rate processes.

docs.title: Pathogen Kinetics
docs.text:
This page is under development.

Documents the pathogen fate and transport process, corresponding to dPathogensdt in v1 nsm1/processes.py. This page will cover first-order pathogen die-off kinetics, including temperature-dependent decay, settling, and light inactivation.

docs.title: Phosphorus
docs.text:
This page is under development.

Documents the phosphorus processes, corresponding to dOrgPdt and dTIPdt in v1 nsm1/processes.py. This page will cover organic phosphorus mineralization, total inorganic phosphorus (TIP) dynamics including algal uptake and release, settling, and sediment phosphorus flux.

docs.title: ClearWater-Riverine
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This section covers ClearWater-Riverine, the hydrodynamic transport engine that reads HEC-RAS HDF output and drives advection-diffusion transport for water quality constituents.

docs.title: Boundary Conditions
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will describe how to specify boundary conditions for ClearWater-Riverine simulations, including inflow concentration time series, open boundaries, and how boundary data maps to the HEC-RAS mesh faces.

docs.title: Riverine Configuration
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will document the YAML configuration file for ClearWater-Riverine, including required fields for the HEC-RAS plan file path, simulation time range, diffusion coefficients, initial conditions, and boundary condition references.

docs.title: Riverine Overview
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will describe the ClearWater-Riverine module, including its role as the hydrodynamic driver, how it reads HEC-RAS 2D unsteady HDF5 plan files, and how it provides flow fields and mesh geometry to downstream water quality modules.

docs.title: Plotting Utilities
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will document the built-in plotting utilities for visualizing ClearWater-Riverine results, including spatial concentration maps on the 2D mesh, time series plots, and animation support.

This page will cover post-processing workflows for ClearWater-Riverine results, including mass balance verification, extracting time series at monitoring points, and exporting results to common formats.

This page will describe the advection-diffusion solver used by ClearWater-Riverine, including the finite-volume discretization on the HEC-RAS 2D mesh, time-stepping scheme, and numerical stability considerations.

docs.title: Temperature Simulation Module (TSM)
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This section covers the Temperature Simulation Module (TSM), which computes water temperature using a surface energy balance approach driven by meteorological forcing data.

docs.title: TSM Configuration
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will document the configuration options for the Temperature Simulation Module, including meteorological input parameters, initial water temperature, and optional calibration coefficients for energy balance terms.

docs.title: Energy Balance Components
docs.text:

This page will detail the individual heat flux terms in the TSM energy balance: net solar radiation, longwave atmospheric radiation, longwave back radiation, evaporative heat loss, conductive heat transfer, and sediment heat flux.

docs.title: TSM Overview
docs.text:
This page is under development.

This page will provide an overview of the Temperature Simulation Module, including the energy balance formulation, required meteorological inputs (air temperature, solar radiation, wind speed, humidity, cloud cover), and the relationship between TSM and downstream water quality modules.
